thread:
evan: forwarding a customer report — after they upgraded their service container to redwood-sdk 1.12 they started getting a hard TypeError in production: `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timeout'`. Happened right after deploy, traffic spike.
maria: do we have a quick repro or stacktrace from them? can you paste the top frames?
evan: stack top looks like: `File \"/srv/app/main.py\", line 42, in handle
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., timeout=30)
TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'timeout'`
alina: thanks. any idea how they installed the sdk? poetry/pip/constraints?
evan: they use Poetry + Docker. from `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes`: `redwood-sdk==1.12.0` and `python 3.10.12`.
maria: ok this aligns with the change we shipped in 1.12 — we removed the legacy constructor alias `timeout` and standardized on `request_timeout` to make parameter names explicit. unfortunately in Python if you pass an unexpected kwarg to our generated client dataclass it raises that TypeError instead of a deprecation warning.
evan: minimal repro I ran locally (docker python:3.10):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=\"x\", timeout=5)
```
-> same TypeError.
alina: for immediate mitigation tell customers to pin to latest 1.11 patch, e.g. `pip install \"redwood-sdk==1.11.4\"` or in pyproject.toml use `redwood-sdk = "1.11.*"` before running `poetry lock`.
maria: we should also provide a short workaround allowing both names until we ship a patch. dev note: change constructor signature to accept `**kwargs` and pop `timeout` into `request_timeout` with a DeprecationWarning.
evan: timeline? customer is on a paid production plan and asking for ETA, they are sensitive (latency critical).
maria: eng-runtime will cut 1.12.1 within ~48h to restore a compatibility shim and add runtime warning. patch will also include a clear Release Note and migration snippet.
alina: creating KB snippet now. suggested support reply (short):
> Hi — we've identified this as a breaking parameter rename in 1.12. Temporary options:
> 1) Pin to 1.11.x: `pip install \"redwood-sdk==1.11.4\"` or `redwood-sdk = "1.11.*"` in pyproject and run `poetry lock`.
> 2) Change your call to `RedwoodClient(..., request_timeout=30)` instead of `timeout=...`.
> We'll release 1.12.1 to restore a compatibility alias within 48 hours; you can upgrade after that.

alina: KB will include these exact commands and a `constraints.txt` example for customers using pip in multi-stage builds:
```
# constraints.txt
redwood-sdk==1.11.4
```

support-bot: incident created: #INC-2026 assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2. :white_check_mark:

maria: follow-ups: add a unit test for constructor kw compatibility, and add a note to the SDK migration guide about `timeout` -> `request_timeout`.
evan: will send customer the pinned-workaround and escalate for credits if needed. closing interim loop here.
